questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Language and proximity to home country

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not that easy, the website of the receiving institution is quite confusing

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: No assistance except for a buddy group which was only active for the welcome day

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very hard, there are a lot of scams and the demand is super high. I waited for my arrival (booked a hostel) and started my search on Idealista and Facebook only then as I wanted to see the room in person. I was lucky but fellow Erasmus students looked for much longer and paid a lot more for a tiny room. Be aware that Barcelona is very expensive in terms of rent.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's better to live off campus as you are more central. I would recommend Gracia or Eixample as those are the safest yet pretty central areas. Avoid Raval area, it's not that safe during the night.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Its easier as a girl, as there are more girls-only dorms available on the renting platforms.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I was send a form to indicate all courses that I wanted to take. I had to change that a couple times due to missing information.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: No help really. The answers for the courses came pretty quick but it took super long till I had a final list of courses since the list of courses on the website was not up to date in the beginning and there was no indication of the course language so I wasn't sure whether it was English or Spanish besides the fully English programs. There was always an issue with a course so I had to get another preapproval like 5 times and send it back to the receiving uni instead of just giving me all available courses to choose.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: pretty unsuccessful as every course I wanted to take outside of the main master program was denied despite adequate knowledge and language skills. There were not many courses left to choose from after considering the schedule etc.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask the international office directly for the schedule and course catalogue (pdf) for the economics and political economy master program so you know directly what the possible options are.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I was not even aware that bachelor courses were an option. (Would have been nice to know as there are more options to choose from then)

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Many more projects which made it hard for me to study the actual content of the course before the exam as you were always busy with some kind of presentation that had little to do with the actual course content. (e.g. research proposals etc.) especially since I had to take double to course load than the full time students. There were participation grades in every course as well which in my opinion does not make sense for master students.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Causes of Global Inequality
Political Behavior
Federalism and Decentralization
Welfare Economics: Education and Social Policies
Policy Evaluation
Creative Cities
Global Sustainability

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Causes of Global Inequality: Interesting, good professors and with two final essays in the end + mandatory readings and participation a manageable workload
Creative Cities

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There's so much outside the uni for general Erasmus students that I did not really inform myself too much on university programs. I wish there were free Spanish classes but only Catalan classes were free. The Spanish classes were actually very expensive so hardly anyone took part.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I am not sure as I mostly took part in other activities outside the university. There are hiking groups, volleyball groups, language exchange groups, etc. for all Erasmus or international students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Beachvolleyball and weekend trips organised by one of the Erasmus groups (find them on social media)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Montserrat, Sitges, Blanes,

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of internationals to pretty easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: that's the hard part. I had a hard time as well and not really successful. They stay among themselves.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing I can think of

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That there is so much so explore, you will not get bored for sure even though sometimes it was a bit overwhelming.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Get social and enjoy being by the ocean (play beachvolleyball!)
Explore areas outside of Barcelona (the city does not have a lot of green areas and is quite congested)
Find a good landlord there are a lot of bad ones around (heard many bad stories)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try to do two terms and divide the workload. It was too much for me in one term

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: living in a vibrant city with a great cuisine and architecture.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Keeping up with the course workload

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
